lines.li: [us] What does a pact mean to your people?
[them,their:tribal] That your fire is ours to defend, and ours is yours.
[them,their:medieval] That your enemies are ours, as long as the oath holds.
[them,their:industrial] That we come when you send for us, and you come when we do.
[them,their:spacer] A mutual obligation, logged on both sides and binding on both.
[them] That neither of us faces trouble alone.
[us] It means much the same to us.
[them] Among my people, those bound by an oath share meat after a hunt.
[us] We'd share ours with you.
[them] Then you understand it better than most outsiders do.
[them] Half the town turned out to witness our side of the oath.
[us] Half the town?
[them] There was ale afterward, which helped.
[them] Our copy of the agreement is pinned up in the quartermaster's office.
[us] Next to what?
[them] Next to the list of people who owe us money, so it's in good company.
[them] Your colony is filed under allies in our records now.
[us] Is that a long list?
[them] Shorter than I'd like, so try to stay on it.
[them] I heard raiders came at your colony.
[us] They did.
[them,lowtech] Next time light your fire early, and we'll come if we can.
[them] Next time send for us early, and we'll come if we can.
[them] The raiders who came at you are no friends of ours either.
[us] Then next time we'll both be glad of the pact.
[them] We're glad of it already.
[them] We keep a watch on your direction now, for smoke or a call.
[us] Would you know it from a cooking fire?
[them] A cooking fire doesn't burn by the gate in the middle of a fight.
[them] {WAR} are at war with both of us, which is half of why we swore.
[us] And the other half?
[them,likesus] My people like yours, mostly.
[them] The other half is that your colony fights well.
[us] If it came to it, would you really come out for us?
[them] I would, and I'd bring my cousins with me.
[us] I hope it never comes to it.
[them] So do I, but it's good to know where we stand.
[us] It is.
[us] Your people are at war with {WAR}, will that keep your fighters busy?
[them] Some of the time, I won't lie to you.
[them] If you call and nobody comes, it won't be because we forgot the pact.
[them] If {TOWN} is ever attacked, my people will write to your colony first.
[us] And we'll send who we can.
[them] Two of yours on the road would be answer enough.
[them] I'd sooner be at home, with a call between our peoples under way.
[us] Why?
[them] Because that's where the news comes first.
[them] We buried some of ours after the fight at your colony.
[us] They died for us, and we know it.
[them] They died for the pact, which to their families is the same thing.
[them] Some of my people would still be alive if your colony fought its own fights.
[us] They came because we'd have come for them.
[them] Our fighters came home from your colony talking about your people.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them] Good things, and that they'd go again if they were called.
[them] When it came to taking sides, your colony took ours.
[us] We had a pact.
[them] Plenty of people have pacts, fewer remember them when it counts.
[them] My people know your colony keeps what it promises.
[us] We try to.
[them,their:tribal] Then the oath between us is a good one, and the elders say so.
[them] That's why my people would keep the pact another year.
[us] Is the cart we send each season what your people want?
[them,trait:Greedy] They'd take twice as much and pay half, if you offered.
[them] They'd take more of it, if you had it to spare.
[us] We'll see what the stores can stand.
[them] Because of the pact, my caravan comes your way each season.
[us] We'll try to make it worth the walk.
[them] Have the good stuff out early and it will be.
[them] At home the goods from your colony are shared out the night they arrive.
[us] Who gets the most?
[them,their:tribal] Whoever carried them, that's only fair.
[them] Whoever paid for them, and then whoever shouts loudest.
[them] The contract's been good for both of us so far.
[us] What would make it better?
[them,their:spacer] Predictable quantities, and fewer surprises in the crates.
[them] A bigger cart, if I'm asked, but nobody asks me.
[them] The trade pact suits my people well enough.
[us] Only well enough?
[them] Your surplus could be better, if you want it straight.
[them] Your stores look thin for a people sending out a cart each season.
[us] If the stores are short, the cart doesn't go.
[them] My people will understand that, better than a cart you can't spare.
[them] Your colony came asking for an oath, and the old ones liked that.
[us] Why?
[them] Because asking is how it's done, and outsiders usually don't.
[them] My people offered your colony the pact, so I'd like to hear it's been worth it.
[us] It has been.
[them] Then I'll say so at home, they'll want to know.
[them] My people will want to know if your colony means to keep the pact another year.
[us] We do, if yours do.
[them] Pact or no pact, I don't have to like you.
[us] No, you only have to come when we call.
[us] Everyone here knows we have friends in {PACTWITH}.
[them] And at home everyone knows we have friends here.
[us] Then that's two places the pact is doing some good.
[them] Your colony broke a pact with my people once.
[us] We know what it cost us.
[them] It cost us more.
[us] Would your people ever swear a pact with us again?
[them,their:tribal] Not while the ones who remember the last one still sit at the fire.
[them] Not soon, and not on the same terms.
[us] That's fair.
